learn.hook: A lump of clay is just mud, until a potter in Khurja turns it into a cup. When does something become a resource?
points: A resource is anything that people can use to meet a need, provided they have the knowledge and technology to use it and it is useful and valued.
Natural resources come from nature, for example air, water, soil, sunlight, forests, minerals and wildlife.
Human-made resources are things people make by changing natural resources, such as roads, bridges, buildings, machines and dams.
People themselves, with their skills, knowledge and health, are a resource too. They are called human resources.
Something can become a resource over time. Petroleum was of little use until people learnt how to refine it and build engines that run on it.

example.q: Think it through: Is the wind blowing over the coast of Tamil Nadu a resource?
steps: Ask: can people use it to meet a need?
Wind can turn the blades of wind turbines and make electricity.
India has the technology to build such turbines, and many stand along that coast.
So people value it and can use it.
example.answer: Yes. Wind is a natural resource because we have the technology to turn it into electricity.

learn.reallife: Every time you drink water, switch on a fan or ride a bus over a bridge, you are using natural or human-made resources.

games.title: Resource or not?
items: A thing becomes a resource only when people can use it and value it.
Usefulness and the ability to use it make something a resource.
A dam is a natural resource.
A dam is built by people, so it is a human-made resource. The river water it stores is natural.
Human skills and knowledge are counted as a resource.
Trained, healthy, educated people are called human resources.
Petroleum has been a valuable resource for people at every point in history.
It became valuable only after people learnt to refine it and use it as fuel.
Soil is a natural resource.
Soil is formed by nature and we use it to grow crops.

quiz.q: Which of these is a human-made resource?
quiz.explain: A cotton mill is built by people. Rivers, coal and sunlight come from nature.
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything useful must be human-made

quiz.q: What turns a natural substance into a resource?
options: People find a use for it and have the technology to use it
quiz.explain: Usefulness, value and the means to use something make it a resource.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rarity or appearance alone makes something a resource

quiz.q: A trained nurse working in a village health centre is an example of a:
quiz.explain: People with skills and knowledge are human resources.
quiz.mistake: Confuses people with things that people make

quiz.q: Which pair has only natural resources?
quiz.explain: Forests and minerals both come from nature without being made by people.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up natural and human-made items

quiz.q: Why is investing in education and health important for a country's resources?
options: It increases the amount of coal in the ground
It improves human resources, the people who use all other resources
It stops the need for any natural resources
quiz.explain: Skilled and healthy people can use and manage other resources better.
quiz.mistake: Does not see people as a resource

quiz.q: Uranium was found in rocks long before it was used to make electricity. When did it become a resource for power?
options: After people developed the technology to use it in nuclear power plants
quiz.explain: A substance becomes a resource for a purpose once people have the knowledge and technology to use it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a substance is a resource only because it exists

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a natural resource?
quiz.explain: A highway is constructed by people, so it is human-made.
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything outdoors is natural

quiz.q: A potter shapes clay from a riverbank into pots. The pots are:
options: Human-made resources made from a natural resource
quiz.explain: Clay is natural; the pots are made by people, so they are human-made resources.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that human-made things come from natural materials

teach.ask: Gappu found a shiny stone and asked, 'Is this a resource?' Explain to Gappu what makes something a resource and the three kinds of resources.
teach.praise: Wow! So a stone is a resource only if we can use it. And people are resources too!
teach.nudge: But what about things that people make, like bridges? And are people a resource?

learn.hook: Sunlight will shine on your terrace tomorrow, but the coal burnt in a power plant today is gone forever. Why the difference?
points: Renewable resources are renewed by nature quickly, within a human lifetime, for example sunlight, wind, water and forests.
Some renewable resources can still run short if we overuse them. Cutting forests faster than they regrow or polluting rivers harms them.
Non-renewable resources take millions of years to form, so once used they cannot be replaced in our lifetime. Coal, petroleum and natural gas are examples.
Coal, petroleum and natural gas are called fossil fuels because they formed from the remains of plants and animals buried long ago.
Resources are spread unevenly. Some regions have plenty of a mineral or of water while others have very little, so regions depend on each other and trade.

example.q: Think it through: A village switches from diesel pumps to solar pumps for watering fields. Which resource is it saving, and why does that matter?
steps: Diesel is made from petroleum, a fossil fuel.
Petroleum takes millions of years to form, so it is non-renewable.
Sunlight is renewed every day, so it is renewable.
Using sunlight saves petroleum for the future and also causes less air pollution.
example.answer: It saves petroleum, a non-renewable resource, by using sunlight, a renewable one.

learn.reallife: The solar panels on rooftops and the wind turbines in Gujarat and Tamil Nadu use renewable resources, while most cars still run on petrol or diesel from petroleum.

items.text: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are called ___ fuels.
Resources that nature renews quickly are called ___ resources.
Fossil fuels take ___ of years to form.
Because resources are spread ___, regions trade with each other.

quiz.q: Which of these is a non-renewable resource?
quiz.explain: Natural gas takes millions of years to form, so it cannot be replaced quickly.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every natural resource is renewable

quiz.q: Why are fossil fuels called non-renewable?
options: They are found only in India
They take millions of years to form
quiz.explain: Their formation is so slow that, once used, they are not replaced within human time.
quiz.mistake: Confuses non-renewable with man-made

quiz.q: Which statement about forests is correct?
options: Forests are renewable but can be destroyed if cut faster than they regrow
quiz.explain: Trees regrow, but overcutting can wipe out a forest.
quiz.mistake: Believes renewable means unlimited

quiz.q: What were fossil fuels formed from?
options: Remains of plants and animals buried long ago
quiz.explain: Buried remains changed slowly under heat and pressure into coal, oil and gas.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the origin of fossil fuels

quiz.q: A region has rich coal deposits but little iron ore. What does uneven distribution of resources often lead to?
options: Every region having the same resources
quiz.explain: When resources are unevenly spread, regions exchange what they have for what they lack.
quiz.mistake: Assumes resources are equally spread everywhere

quiz.q: Which energy source is renewable?
quiz.explain: The Sun keeps giving light and heat every day.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up common fuels with renewable sources

quiz.q: Groundwater is renewed by rain, yet wells in some places are drying up. Why?
options: Water is being pumped out faster than rain can refill it
Wells always dry up in winter
quiz.explain: Even a renewable resource runs short if it is used faster than nature renews it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks renewable resources can never run short

quiz.q: Which group contains only fossil fuels?
quiz.explain: These three formed underground from ancient remains over millions of years.
quiz.mistake: Mixes renewable sources with fossil fuels

teach.ask: Gappu thinks everything in nature will last forever. Explain renewable and non-renewable resources to Gappu.
teach.praise: Oh no, coal cannot come back quickly! I will cheer for the sun and the wind.
teach.nudge: Can you give me examples? Which ones run out, and which ones come back?

learn.hook: If you eat all the mangoes on a tree and also chop the tree down, what will you eat next summer?
points: Sustainable use means using resources to meet our needs today without harming the ability of future generations to meet their needs.
Overuse and waste harm resources: cutting forests, over-pumping groundwater, overfishing and polluting rivers are examples.
We can conserve resources with the 3 Rs: Reduce what we use, Reuse things, and Recycle materials.
Many Indian communities have long protected nature, for example sacred groves, rainwater harvesting in stepwells and tanks, and the Bishnoi tradition of protecting trees and animals.
Mahatma Gandhi's idea is often quoted: the Earth provides enough to satisfy every person's need, but not every person's greed.

example.q: Think it through: A school in Chennai collects rainwater from its roof into an underground tank. How is this sustainable?
steps: Rain that falls on the roof would otherwise run off into drains.
The tank stores it, or lets it soak into the ground to refill groundwater.
The school pumps less groundwater for gardening and cleaning.
Groundwater is saved for the future.
example.answer: Rainwater harvesting saves and refills groundwater, so the resource lasts for the future.

learn.reallife: Switching off fans when you leave a room, carrying a cloth bag to the market and giving old books to younger students are all ways to use resources sustainably.

games.title: Match the action to the idea
pairs: Using a steel bottle instead of buying plastic bottles
Using old jam jars to store spices
Sending old newspapers to be made into new paper
Collecting rain from the roof in a tank

games.title: Sustainable or not?
items: Fishing so much in one season that fish cannot breed is sustainable.
Overfishing leaves too few fish to breed, so the catch falls in later years.
Sustainable use means thinking about the needs of future generations.
That is the core idea of sustainable development.
Recycling paper can reduce the number of trees cut for new paper.
Used paper is turned into new paper, so less fresh wood pulp is needed.
The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan is known for protecting trees and wild animals.
Protecting trees and animals such as blackbuck is part of their tradition.
Leaving lights on in an empty room saves electricity.
It wastes electricity; switching them off saves it.

quiz.q: Which best describes sustainable use of resources?
options: Meeting today's needs without harming future generations' ability to meet theirs
Using as much as possible now
quiz.explain: Sustainable use balances present needs with the needs of the future.
quiz.mistake: Thinks sustainability means not using resources at all

quiz.q: Carrying a cloth bag instead of taking a new plastic bag each time is an example of:
quiz.explain: You are reducing the number of plastic bags used.
quiz.mistake: Confuses reducing with recycling

quiz.q: Sacred groves found in many parts of India help to:
options: Protect patches of forest and their plants and animals
quiz.explain: Communities have traditionally protected these groves, keeping trees and wildlife safe.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect traditions with conservation

quiz.q: Which practice harms a renewable resource?
options: Pumping groundwater faster than rain can refill it
quiz.explain: Over-pumping makes water tables fall, even though water is renewable.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only non-renewable resources can be harmed

quiz.q: 'The Earth provides enough to satisfy every man's need, but not every man's greed.' Whose idea is this?
quiz.explain: This saying is widely credited to Mahatma Gandhi.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up national leaders

quiz.q: Old plastic bottles melted and made into new products is an example of:
quiz.explain: Recycling changes used material into new products.
quiz.mistake: Confuses recycling with reusing

quiz.q: Why is switching to solar power considered good for sustainability?
options: It uses a renewable source and causes less pollution
quiz.explain: Sunlight is renewable and solar panels do not burn fuel.
quiz.mistake: Does not link energy choices with sustainability

quiz.q: Riya's family fixes a dripping tap at once. What are they conserving?
quiz.explain: A dripping tap can waste many litres of water every day.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice everyday waste of water

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know why grown-ups keep saying 'save water, save electricity'. Explain sustainable use to Gappu.
teach.praise: I get it now! Use what we need, waste nothing, and leave enough for the little birds of the future.
teach.nudge: But why should we care about later? And what are some ways to save resources?
